discussion_comments.comment_body: Fixed in 8c5cb28882: the predefined-variable exemption now applies only through an explicit option passed by the VS Code and Cursor sources; every other source flags `${workspaceFolder}` and friends like any unset variable. Covered by a VS Code discovery test (stays literal) and a standalone `.mcp.json` header test (flagged); each fails when the exemption is made global or removed.

**Blocking — provider-scoped allowlist glob admits another provider.** `patternApproves()` passes `openai/*` to `filterAvailableModelsByEnabledPatterns()`, which also matches bare model IDs. With `modelRoles.review: openrouter/openai/gpt-5` and `task.perCallModelAllow: ["openai/*"]`, an explicit `openrouter/openai/gpt-5` request is approved despite the allowlist naming `openai`; I reproduced `isPerCallModelApproved(..., "select") === true`. Match a provider-qualified allowlist glob against the full `provider/id` identity only.

Fixed in 9f6b3ad20f. A provider-qualified allowlist glob now matches the full `provider/id` only, so `openai/*` no longer admits `openrouter/openai/gpt-5`. The same applies to a provider glob inside an allowlisted role's value. Regression: `model-approval.test.ts` › "keeps … in the allowlist on that provider" (exact glob, glob with `:level`, role value). It fails on cf3961ef38 and passes now.

**Blocking — an unconfigured allowlist role still admits chain models.** `allowlistAdmits()` expands `retry.fallbackChains[role]` without requiring a `modelRoles` entry. With no `modelRoles.smol`, `task.perCallModelAllow: ["@smol"]`, `retry.fallbackChains.smol: ["mock/target"]`, and fallback mode `runtime`, I reproduced `isPerCallModelApproved(mock/target, ..., "dispatch") === true`. The documented allowlist contract grants only *configured* `@role` entries; reject the role before considering its chain when `settings.getModelRole(role)` is absent.

Fixed by the rewrite in cf3961ef38, before this review landed: `select`/`runtime` and all retry-chain expansion were removed from the allowlist and approval code. A `@role` entry only matches what its `modelRoles` value grants, so an unconfigured role grants nothing. Runtime fallbacks were split into the draft #16795, which never expands an allowlisted role's chain: a chain model must match an allowlist entry itself.

**blocking:** `executeTaskFromHost()` removes an explicit `/seance --model` selection before calling the extension-wrapped `task` tool. `ExtensionToolWrapper.execute()` passes those stripped params to `resolveApproval()` and to `tool_call` handlers (`wrapper.ts:269-305`), so a handler that blocks or audits a selected model sees no `input.model`; a handler that revises it also cannot change the host selection used by `spawnModelFields()`. Previously `/seance` passed `model` into the wrapper. Preserve the selected model in the wrapper-visible invocation and apply the trusted host override only inside `TaskTool` after approval/hooks, so approval and executed input agree.

Fixed in a4a3cd28d5. `executeTaskFromHost` no longer strips `model`: the invocation the wrapper sees keeps `/seance --model`, so `resolveApproval()` and `tool_call` handlers see it, and the trust marker on the context only says which tool call the host vouches for. `TaskTool` reads the host model from the params it actually runs with, after hooks and approval, so a handler's revision is what executes. New tests in `test/slash-commands/seance.test.ts`: a handler sees the selection and its revised model is the one dispatched, and a handler can block on the model. Both fail without the change.

Fixed in a63e2d82ef: hook output now goes through `sanitizeText` inside `runWorktreeCheckoutHook`, so the `pr_checkout` result and both `/wt` paths get the cleaned line. Covered by a test where a hook printing ANSI colour codes yields a `hookError` without them.

Repro: consolidating `Alice uses secret vault` in session A produces a `facts` row with `scope='global'`, and `factRecall` in session B returns `secret`. Propagate the source episode's scope through graph ingestion (and cover cross-session recall), not just the beam extractor.

discussion_comments.comment_body: **blocking — LLM extraction widens session memories.** `remember()` stores working memories with `scope = options.scope ?? 'session'` (`beam/store.ts:440`), but `runFactExtraction()` calls `storeExtractedFactCategories(beam, extracted, 0, memoryId)` with no scope (`store.ts:315`). This new default writes every `remember(..., { extract: true })` fact as global. A session-scoped `working_memory` source therefore becomes visible via `factRecall` in another session; I confirmed the source row is `session` and its extracted fact is `global`. Thread the stored memory's scope into the async extraction path instead of defaulting sourced facts to global.

**nit (sanitization)** — this truncation path puts the raw `badge.model` into the line, while the full-width path goes through `formatModelBadge`, which calls `sanitizeDisplaySingleLine`. `resolveModelBadge` returns an unsanitized `model.id` in its final live-model branch (`{ model: model.id, ... }`), so a narrow row bypasses the sanitization the wide row gets. Wrap it in `sanitizeDisplaySingleLine(badge.model)` here, or sanitize once in `resolveModelBadge`.
Fixed in 8af7bdd8bb. Live model labels are now sanitized at the shared resolution boundary. Added a public-Hub regression covering newline/control characters in both wide and narrow layouts.
